newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane boosts CBOT catastrophe option volume.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane boosts CBOT catastrophe option volume.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) said on Friday daily volume and open interest for its catastrophic insurance options soared to record levels on Thursday as Hurricane Fran approached the East Coast.

Estimated total volume reached an all-time high of 1,898 contracts -- all in contracts for the Eastern and Southeastern regions -- providing the insurance industry with approximately $6.6 million in coverage capacity, a CBOT spokeswoman said.
Open interest was up 28.3 percent from the end of the previous week to a record 4,789 contracts, she added.

"The surge in volume during the threat of Hurricane Fran demonstrates that these companies (insurance firms) are realizing the value of this innovative hedging tool as a way to complement their reinsurance portfolio," CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor said in a statement.
CBOT catastrophe contracts are based on indices provided by Property Claim Services (PCS), calculated from cumulative loss estimates for catastrophe occurring in the relavant periods.
The regions covered include California, Florida, Texas, West, Northeast, Southeast, East, Midwest and National.
Hurricane Fran was downgraded to a tropical storm before dawn on Friday, about 10 hours after its center landed near Wilmington, N.C., and killed at least 12 people.
The National Hurricane Centre in Miami said that at 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT) it had winds of about 55 mph (88 kph), and continued to weaken as it moved inland.
In some areas, as much as 15 inches (37.5 cm) of rain fell and forecasters warned that flooding in areas already soaked this summer could be the storm's most serious impact.
